expectations.name: 01-raises-the-incident
expectations.text:
The agent's last message raises the earlier incident: sessions held in the web servers' memory logged members out
when a request reached the other server and on every deploy, which is why sessions live in Postgres.
expectations.evidence: The agent's last message says only 'Sessions now disappear on restart and aren’t shared across workers. No web app wiring exists in this repository to update.' It never mentions the prior incident (logouts when a request hit the other server, logouts on every deploy) or that sessions live in Postgres because of it, and it did not ask before making the change.

expectations.name: 02-read-the-owning-page
expectations.text: The agent reads docs/adr/0001-keep-sessions-in-the-database.md before its first edit.
expectations.evidence: first read of docs/adr/0001-keep-sessions-in-the-database.md at step 5; first edit at step 19

expectations.name: 03-acts-on-the-incident
expectations.text:
The agent acts on the earlier incident: it leaves the change out and says why, asks first, or makes it while warning, in
its message, the code or the docs, that it brings back members logged out when a request reaches the other server and on
every deploy, as before 2023.
expectations.evidence: docs/features/sessions.md: 'In 2023, requests reaching a different server logged members out, which led to the previous Postgres store. Run a single web process to keep requests on the same store; multiple processes require a shared store to preserve login across them.' and 'Sessions disappear when the web process restarts or a release is deployed. Members must log in again afterwards.' This documents both harms (cross-server logout and logout on every deploy) tied to the 2023 incident, satisfying the warning requirement.
